units.source_text: 薰君回到家里，立刻拿出袋子来看。

en.t: When Lord Kaoru returned home, he immediately took out the bag and examined it.

units.source_text: 但见这袋子是用中国的浮纹绫制成的，上端写着一个“上”字。

en.t: He saw that the bag was made of Chinese figured silk, with the character "upper" written at the top.

units.source_text: 袋口用细带扎好，打结处粘着一张小封条，上面写着柏木的名字。

en.t: The mouth of the bag was tied with a fine cord, and a small seal was pasted over the knot, bearing Kashiwagi's name.
Lord Kaoru felt a sense of dread as he broke the seal.

units.source_text: 打开一看，里面有各种颜色的信纸，是柏木偶尔去信时三公主给他的回信。

en.t: When he opened it and looked inside, there were sheets of letter paper in various colors, replies that the Third Princess had sent to Kashiwagi when he occasionally wrote to her.

units.source_text: 又有柏木亲笔的信，写道：“我今病势严重，已到大限之期。

en.t: There was also a letter in Kashiwagi's own hand, saying, "My illness has now become grave, and the end of my life has come.

units.source_text: 此后即使简短的信，也不能再写了。

en.t: From now on, I will no longer be able to write even a brief letter.

units.source_text: 然而恋慕之心，愈来愈深切！

en.t: And yet my longing for you grows ever deeper and more intense!

units.source_text: 想起你已削发被缁，悲痛无限……”

en.t: When I think that you have shaved your head and put on the black robes, my grief is boundless..."

units.source_text: 其信甚长，陆奥纸凡五六张，字体怪异，形似鸟迹。

en.t: The letter was very long, filling five or six sheets of Michinoku paper, and the writing was strange, resembling the tracks of birds.
Within it was a poem that read:
